Reload the page, then use the retry control: it sends the original identifier, payload and expected revision, confirms the same acceptance and does not apply the discard twice. Read the latest table after confirmation. For the stale-receipt case, accept the other seat's discard from another page before retrying: the recovered page must display the latest two-discard state, not roll back to the earlier receipt. Valid play remains possible after recovery. If interception failed to forward/abort as specified, record a setup error and repeat once; never retry a demonstrated app defect into a pass.
criteria.reasoning: Forward-and-abort proved the server accepted the discard and the UI initially showed Retry Move, but after the required reload the retry control disappeared, so safe UI recovery could not be completed.

criteria.name: recovery_phase_matrix
criteria.description:
Setup: prepare separate games paused after one discard; both discards (automatic cut is allowed); a go/reset; and the completed show before Next hand. Also retain a finished game, the accepted create and winning-action requests from the replay checks, and a Club night series paused between hands. Record both seat-filtered states for every game, revisions, ladder, summaries and all identities. If a prerequisite capture is unavailable, build your own independent valid case rather than inheriting another criterion's failure.
Reload/reopen the unfinished games through their chooser and compare every saved phase, cards, privacy, count, turn, score and revision. Use bash /tests/app-lifecycle.sh restart once for this matrix, without reseeding or edits. Reopen and compare again; finished results/counters and all unrelated games remain unchanged. Retry the captured create and winning action with their exact original identities after restart: original acceptance, no duplicates. Continue one legal action in each unfinished game; the series must deal its next prescribed round with the correct alternating dealer. Compare relative current baselines and ignore incidental timestamps. This is a real process restart, not merely page reload.
criteria.reasoning: After one helper restart, chooser reopen matched all recorded phase/privacy/revision states; exact create and winning retries were idempotent, legal continuations worked, and the club series advanced to hand 2 with B dealer.

criteria.name: keyboard_controls_and_focus
criteria.description:
Setup: use the visible game controls, seat switcher and scoring bench with the keyboard.
Require labels/accessible names for starting, choosing cards, discarding and any supplied cut/count controls. Automatic cutting/counting does not require an additional manual button. Tab/Shift+Tab show visible focus; Enter/Space operate cards and buttons; focus after a card action remains on a useful reachable control. No keyboard trap or unintended game mutation from moving focus. Inspect landmarks/headings where applicable; do not demand a navigation landmark when the app has no navigation.
criteria.reasoning: Accessible names were present for starting, cards, discarding, seat switching, and bench controls. Enter/Space worked; focus outlines were visible and card focus remained after selection.

criteria.name: responsive_controls_and_reachability
criteria.description: Inspect at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760. Through normal vertical scrolling, reach the board, active hand, crib/play controls, saved-game chooser, bench and ladder. No horizontal page overflow, clipped essential label or inaccessible action. Card controls and touch targets remain practical. Grade reachability/operability, not decorative composition.
criteria.reasoning: At 375×760 the document overflowed horizontally (scrollWidth 424 vs 375); saved-game tables extended to about 803px and ladder history was offscreen. Desktop 1280×800 fit.

criteria.name: illegal_move_feedback
criteria.description:
Setup: start P at zero and play B:5S,A:7H,B:6H,A:TH to reach 28 with B to act. Try B:9D or inspect its disabled-state explanation.
Require a visible textual reason for the over-31 refusal, readable/announced feedback and a still-usable table. Valid B:AC afterward must work. Feedback must not depend solely on red colour or a silent disabled button. Observe actual UI outcomes; exact response codes are not prescribed.
criteria.reasoning: At count 28, 9D was disabled as “unplayable,” but had no textual reason, title, description, or live announcement explaining that it would exceed 31. Valid AC still worked.

criteria.name: pending_action_and_empty_state
criteria.description:
Setup: open the root without selecting a saved game, then start your own zero-score game.
The no-game view has a usable, labelled control to start a game; a plain board
with a New game button is sufficient. Explanatory empty-state prose is optional. During a real pending game save, rapid repeated activation of that same control must not create duplicate accepted actions/games; show a busy/pending state or suppress repeated activation. Hold the first real game POST pending with browser network interception, confirm it is still pending, then attempt repeated mouse and keyboard activation before releasing it. Record request/response timing, accepted game IDs and observed busy state. Two clicks after separate completed saves do not test this requirement. Do not alter payloads or fabricate success. If the first request was never held, that is a setup error, not proof of a duplicate-action defect. Resume/close controls and any supplied panels leave the surrounding table usable. Do not require dialogs the app does not have.
criteria.reasoning: The no-game/practice view had a usable “Start Game at Table” control. However, while the first game POST remained pending, repeated mouse and keyboard activation produced another accepted 201 response and duplicate unfinished game IDs.

criteria.name: readable_state_and_reduced_motion
criteria.description:
Setup: inspect an active zero-score P game, its show and scoring bench, then emulate reduced motion.
Names, active seat, dealer, turn, hand number, cut, count, scores and scoring commentary are available as text alongside the SVG. Bench totals and separate scoring categories remain readable and clearly separate from ranked game points. Show entries remain readable until Next hand. Nonessential motion is reduced or already absent; no information is lost. Grade semantic clarity and motion support, not visual taste or rechecking score arithmetic.
criteria.reasoning: Dealer, hand, stage, active seat, cut, count, turn, scores, show entries, and scoring commentary were exposed as text. Bench totals/categories were separate and readable; reduced-motion emulation reduced durations to near-zero without losing information.

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess rendered table, game, scoring bench, ladder and show typography at desktop size.
5: deliberate, readable type sizes and weights distinguish product title,
seat, turn/result, totals and secondary history; alignment is consistent.
4: readable with one or two minor sizing or alignment imperfections.
3: noticeable inconsistent sizing, crowding or awkward text truncation.
2: several important labels or history entries are difficult to read.
1: broadly illegible, misaligned or undifferentiated text.
0: no coherent typographic rendering on the reviewed surfaces.
Do not grade move correctness or exact seed values here.
criteria.reasoning: Readable, deliberate type hierarchy across the table, game state, scoring bench, ladder, history, and show; titles, seats, totals, stage labels, and secondary details are clearly differentiated.

criteria.name: visual_color_and_contrast
criteria.description:
Assess the supplied theme; a theme switcher is not required. Suit colours are
not prescribed: monochrome, two-colour and four-colour decks are all permitted.
5: cohesive palette with clearly distinguishable suit symbols and both peg tracks, face-down
cards, legible text and purposeful accents across game, scoring bench and show.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: some low-contrast text or conflicting accents distract from the board.
2: substantial legibility or piece-distinction problems.
1: widespread low contrast or harsh, incoherent color treatment.
0: no readable color treatment renders.
Judge appearance, not actual winner detection or accessible-name behavior.
criteria.reasoning: Cohesive dark green/navy theme with strong gold and cyan accents, readable text, distinct red/black suit symbols, patterned face-down cards, and visibly differentiated peg tracks.

criteria.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
criteria.description:
Assess spacing on desktop table, peg board, cards, scoring bench, ladder and show.
5: consistent margins and alignment, deliberate board/control grouping and
balanced spacing between totals, history and show.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several crowded, drifting or excessively separated elements.
2: frequent collisions, clipping or inconsistent gutters.
1: broadly unbalanced or broken layout.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders.
Do not require a specific arrangement or the reference's pixels.
criteria.reasoning: Desktop layouts use consistent gutters, aligned cards, grouped controls, balanced score panels, and well-separated show breakdown sections without collisions or clipping.

criteria.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
criteria.description:
Assess how easily the board, turn/result, seat, scores, commentary and scoring breakdown can be
visually located on desktop without reading all surrounding text.
5: clear visual order with primary game state prominent and related secondary
information grouped; the scoring bench is clearly distinct from the active game.
4: mostly clear with minor competing emphasis.
3: several competing sections or important information visually buried.
2: headings, controls and content are difficult to distinguish.
1: little usable visual order.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders.
Functional correctness and keyboard traversal are outside this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Primary game state, stage, active seat, totals, pegging count, scoring bench, ladder headings, and show totals are easy to locate and visually grouped.

criteria.name: visual_overall_craft
criteria.description:
Assess visual consistency across table, game, scoring bench, ladder and show.
5: one deliberate component language, integrated board-game identity and
finished treatment of history, empty states and secondary controls.
4: one or two minor inconsistent details.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent components between surfaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or disconnected.
1: little considered component styling.
0: no crafted presentation renders.
Do not require branding, decorative assets or features absent from the brief.
criteria.reasoning: The surfaces share a finished board-game component language, including custom cards, peg board, empty states, event history, reference examples, and detailed show breakdowns. The working-table gate also passed with successful local data responses, no console errors, and a fresh server read retaining the accepted discards.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Compare screenshots at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760 for table, game, scoring bench, ladder and show.
5: typography, palette, component styling and hierarchy remain visually
coherent while the layout adapts naturally to each viewport.
4: minor visual inconsistency at one size.
3: visible uneven scaling, crowding or loss of hierarchy between sizes.
2: substantial visual fragmentation at the narrow size.
1: barely coherent presentation at one size.
0: no reviewable presentation at either size.
Score visual adaptation only; control reachability/overflow is graded by
Polish. Ordinary vertical scrolling is allowed; missing required surfaces
are not waived or treated as full-credit evidence.
criteria.reasoning: The mobile table, navigation, cards, and scoring bench adapt coherently, but the ladder remains a wide two-column desktop layout with match history beginning offscreen, and the mobile show panel slightly exceeds the viewport. This creates visible horizontal overflow and loss of secondary-surface hierarchy at 375px.
